Half-Life was a major success. Half-Life 2 even moreso, and its expansion packs (Episode One and Two) were also well received. Did gamers not pump money into Valve by purchasing these games? Why has Valve taken so damn long to develop HL3, and why won't they make a definitive statement about it?
ELI5: Why didn't Valve make HL3 as quickly as possible? Wouldn't it be in their best interest to sell this game to their legion of fans?

The Hype for the game is too much. They can release another great game like 1 and 2 but will it live up to the hype. If it does Valve will have not only the best game ever but also all the money it could ever want. If it doesn't fans will lose their adoration for the company and the game series along with it. People will no longer judge valve on how great of a job they are doing with all their games but on how bad people perceived HL3 to be. Valve knows that either their game comes out perfect or it will be a bust and honestly this day in age when was the last time a game came out perfect and bug free?

Valve doesn't work like that, there are no business men forcing them to release games that would possibly make profit. They make the games they want to make and apparently no one at Valve wants the game enough to start developing it.

why won't they make a definitive statement about it

Gabe has made the statement several times that no one is developing it. Why would they need to hold a press conference every time they are not doing something?
I think I remember gabe saying they were working on it a while back. I'm sure its been in development forever.

He said that no one was working on it and saw no reason for it either in a podcast in March.

Here's the pertinent quote:

The only reason we’d go back and do like a super classic kind of product is if a whole bunch of people just internally at Valve said they wanted to do it and had a reasonable explanation for why…. If you want to do another Half-Life game and you want to ignore everything we’ve learned in shipping Portal 2 and in shipping all the updates on the multiplayer side, that seems like a bad choice.

Valve has a management style which could be called flat. There is no real bosses or teams in the classical sense, projects are developed based on the interests of the individuals involved. I'm sure a lot of Valves staff would be interested in working on HL3 and probably have worked on it in one form or another but other commitments might come first which means HL3 has less overall priority within the company.

Brace yourselves what what is likely to be a dumb question. If I click on one of the donotlink.com links I see here, I will be taken to Freethought Blogs, right? If donotlink.com works the way I think it does, using these links deprives them of the added SEO boost a regular link would involve. But if I click on one, I'm still contributing to their traffic, aren't I?
Well, according to donotlink.com, no, you do not provide a boost to their traffic. Specifically, it says on the front page: "Link without improving "their" search engine position"

I guess I'm not sure how visiting their page would not contribute to their traffic. I think the text you quoted refers to not giving them an incoming link, which is different from the traffic that comes from actually visiting the site. Not improving their search engine position through an incoming link is nice, but it still seems like sharing links to their site will increase their traffic when anyone clicks on the links.

This is completely incorrect

Suppose you've got a blog. You post a link on your blog back to an SJW page to criticize them. Google crawls your page, sees the link to the SJW page, and says "Ok, someone linked back to this SJW page. That page must be important, so let's boost their rankings in our database." Merely by linking to them, you've improved their search engine position.

DoNotLink does three things.

  1. It adds this link to the block list in DoNotLink's robots.txt file. This tells search engines to ignore it when they crawl DoNotLink.com.
  2. They set the "nofollow" attribute on the link. This also tells search engines they should ignore the link.
  3. They keep a database of search engine crawlers. If a crawler tries to access a DoNotLink link, they are directed to a blank error page instead of the linked content. When you try to visit it, however, it checks your IP address against their blacklist, and when it doesn't find it, they go ahead and forward you to the target of the link.

What this all means is that DoNotLink DOES NOT PREVENT THEM FROM RECEIVING TRAFFIC. They still serve the content to you directly. They still get credit for ad impressions. They still see your traffic. Furthermore, If they use Google Analytics, for example, Google sees that traffic, and Google use that information to improve their search engine position.

The ONLY thing that DoNotLink does is prevent search engines from seeing that you linked directly back to the SJW page you're criticizing. A DoNotLink link will still drive your audience to their page, earning them money and improving their search engine position through observation of that incoming traffic.

I just read up on this subject, and I think I may finally have the answer. What donotlink does is prevent links from boosting a site's search engine rankings. This is certainly a good thing in the sense that it stops links from contributing to a site's search engine traffic. What it does not do, though, is prevent the site from receiving traffic when someone clicks on the link. So basically, every time someone clicks on one of those donotlink links to FtB, they benefit from the incoming traffic in the same way the would when someone clicks a regular link. To prevent that, one would need to use something like archive.org so that clicking on the link took one somewhere besides their site.
